column1: # Casks that don't go in a batch upgrade. Waypoint's Updates tab lists them apart from the rest,
# and bump.zsh walks you through each one.
#   accessibility, input-monitoring  hooks keyboard or mouse input. A new binary loses its grant, and
#                                    an unanswered re-prompt can wedge every click (21 Oct, 1 Nov)
#   admin                            asks for an admin password
#   terminal-app                     runs in Terminal.app rather than iTerm

column3: Hooks the menu bar, so its new binary needs Accessibility granted again
Remaps the keyboard, so its new binary needs Input Monitoring granted again, and its installer asks for an admin password
Hooks the media keys, so its new binary needs Accessibility granted again. Its unanswered re-prompt wedged every click on 21 Oct
Hooks the keyboard, so its new binary needs Accessibility granted again. Its re-prompt wedged the trackpad after a reboot on 1 Nov
Moves windows, so its new binary needs Accessibility granted again
Asks for an admin password for its privileged helper
A pkg install, which asks for an admin password
Runs in Terminal.app, since upgrading iTerm takes down the iTerm window running it. Terminal.app needs App Management for it
